Find the first three non-zero terms of the Taylor expansion of e−x3 about x=−1.

a
e−x3=e−3e(x+1)−16e3(x+1)2+⋯
b
e−x3=1e+2e(x+1)+163e(x+1)2+⋯
c
e−x3=e−3e(x+1)+15e2(x+1)2+⋯
d
e−x3=e+2e(x+1)+4e3(x+1)2+⋯
e
e−x3=1e−3e(x+1)+152e(x+1)2+⋯
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We use Taylor's theorem in the form f(x)=f(a)+f′(a)(x−a)+f″(a)2!(x−a)2+f‴(a)3!(x−a)3+⋯, with f(x)=e−x3 and a=−1.

Computing the required derivatives, we have

f(x)=e−x3f(−1)=e−(−1)3=ef′(x)=−3x2e−x3f′(−1)=−3(−1)2e−(−1)3=−3ef″(x)=(−3x2)⋅(−3x2)⋅e−x3+(−6x)⋅e−x3=(9x4−6x)e−x3f″(−1)=(9⋅(−1)4−6⋅(−1))e−(−1)3=15e.

Therefore, e−x3=e+(−3e)(x+1)+15e2!(x+1)2+⋯=e−3e(x+1)+15e2(x+1)2+⋯.
